name: The Waterworks
chemistry: Elements, atoms, chemical formulas and molecules

dialogue: Ah! Another apprentice scientist! Excellent timing. The laboratory is in quite a predicament!
You see, everything around us is made of atoms. Even these stone blocks!
An ELEMENT is a substance made of only one kind of atom. Hydrogen and oxygen are elements.
Unfortunately, our water generator has stopped working. Perhaps you can help me restore it?
Remember: water contains TWO hydrogen atoms and ONE oxygen atom. That's H₂O!
Hydrogen crystals glow pale blue in the east wall. Oxygen ore glows red in the west wall.
Hold LEFT CLICK on a deposit to mine it. Then bring the atoms to the crafting table and give it a try!

steps.hint: Hydrogen crystals glow pale blue in the east (right) wall. Oxygen ore glows red in the west (left) wall. Hold left click to mine.
reminder: Look for the glowing deposits! Blue hydrogen crystals on the east wall, red oxygen ore on the west wall.
Hold left click on a deposit until it breaks.

steps.text: Craft Water (H₂O) at the crafting table
steps.hint: Right click the crafting table in the middle of the room. Put 2 H and 1 O anywhere in the 3×3 grid.
reminder: The crafting table is a molecule modeler. Place two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in the grid.
The arrangement doesn't matter — only the number of each kind of atom!

steps.text: Pour the water into the generator
steps.textNeedItem: Craft Water (H₂O), then use it on the generator
steps.hint: The water generator is the metal machine by the west wall, next to me. Right click it while you have Water.
reminder: Bring the water to the generator beside me and right click it!

dialogue: Splendid! Listen to that water flow! Before the gate opens, a quick check for my new apprentice...

complete: Wonderful! The water wheel turns the gears, and the gears lift the gate!
Keep your water model safe in your Discoveries book. Onward to the Crystal Caverns!
idle: Water is the most common compound on Earth's surface. H₂O — two hydrogens, one oxygen!
The Crystal Caverns are just through the gate. Dr. Salty will be delighted to see you.

name: The Crystal Caverns
chemistry: Elements versus compounds, chemical formulas and mixtures

dialogue: Welcome to the Crystal Caverns! Beautiful, aren't they?
Unfortunately, the frozen gate has trapped us inside.
Perhaps some salt could help. Salt can lower the freezing point of water!
But first, you'll need to discover what elements make up table salt.
Table salt is sodium chloride: NaCl. It is a COMPOUND — two different elements chemically combined.
Sodium crystals sparkle lavender on the west side. Chlorine crystals glow yellow-green on the east side.

steps.hint: Sodium crystals (Na) are lavender, west side of the cave. Chlorine crystals (Cl) are yellow-green, east side.
reminder: NaCl has one sodium and one chlorine. Find a sodium crystal to the west and a chlorine crystal to the east.

steps.hint: Use the crafting table in the middle of the cave. NaCl means 1 Na and 1 Cl.
reminder: No subscripts in NaCl means a 1:1 ratio — one sodium for every chlorine.

steps.text: Sprinkle salt on the frozen gate
steps.textNeedItem: Craft Sodium Chloride (NaCl), then use it on the frozen gate
steps.hint: The frozen gate is at the far north end of the cave. Right click the ice while carrying salt.
reminder: Take your salt to the frozen gate in the north and right click the ice!

dialogue: Look at that ice melt! Salt dissolves into the thin layer of water on the ice and lowers its freezing point.
Let's make sure that salty knowledge sticks!

complete: The gate is free! Salt water freezes at a lower temperature than pure water.
That's why salt trucks spread salt on icy roads in winter. Off you go — the Carbon Caverns await!
idle: Saltwater is a MIXTURE: the salt and water are not chemically combined. Evaporate the water and the salt is left behind!
Sodium is a reactive metal and chlorine is a poisonous gas — yet together they make harmless salt. Chemistry is amazing!

name: The Carbon Caverns

dialogue: Careful! My carbonation machine has broken down!
Without pressure in the pipes, the door to the Limestone Ruins will never open. A tragedy!
If we can create carbon dioxide, we can restore the machine and activate the next door.
Carbon dioxide contains one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms. Think you can craft it?
Carbon deposits are dark lumps in the west wall. Oxygen ore glows red in the east wall.

steps.hint: Carbon deposits are the dark lumps along the west wall. Oxygen ore is in the east wall.
reminder: CO₂: one carbon, two oxygen. The little 2 is a subscript!

steps.hint: The crafting table is in the center of the cavern. The 2 in CO₂ belongs to oxygen.
reminder: Count carefully: the subscript 2 after O means two oxygen atoms.

steps.text: Load CO₂ into the carbonation machine
steps.textNeedItem: Craft Carbon Dioxide (CO₂), then load it into the carbonation machine
steps.hint: The carbonation machine is in the north-west corner with glass pipes on top.
reminder: Quickly! The carbonation machine is in the north-west corner.

dialogue: BUBBLES! Glorious bubbles! The pressure is rising!
Now, prove that you truly understand subscripts...

complete: Remember: CO and CO₂ are different substances. Change the number of atoms and you change the substance!
idle: You breathe out carbon dioxide with every breath. Plants breathe it in to make sugar. A perfect partnership!
The Limestone Ruins are ancient. Dr. Calcite knows everything about them.

name: The Limestone Ruins
chemistry: Compounds, formula units, and physical versus chemical changes

dialogue: Ah, a visitor. Welcome to the Limestone Ruins. Mind the chasm — the old bridge collapsed long ago.
These ruins are made of limestone, which is mostly calcium carbonate: CaCO₃.
Calcium carbonate is found in limestone, chalk, seashells and even eggshells.
Our stone fabricator can rebuild the bridge if you give it a calcium carbonate model as a blueprint.
CaCO₃ has one calcium, one carbon and THREE oxygen atoms. Calcium ore is in the west cavern, carbon in the east cavern, and oxygen in this hall's west wall.

steps.hint: Explore the side caverns: calcium ore in the WEST cavern, carbon in the EAST cavern. Oxygen ore is in the hall's west wall.
reminder: CaCO₃: 1 calcium, 1 carbon, 3 oxygen. The side caverns hold what you need.

steps.hint: Use the crafting table in the hall. CaCO₃ contains 5 atoms in one formula unit.
reminder: Remember: the 3 only belongs to oxygen. One calcium, one carbon, three oxygen.

steps.text: Insert CaCO₃ into the stone fabricator
steps.textNeedItem: Craft Calcium Carbonate (CaCO₃), then insert it into the fabricator
steps.hint: The stone fabricator stands west of the broken bridge.
reminder: The fabricator is beside the chasm. Right click it with your calcium carbonate.

dialogue: Look — the bridge rebuilds itself, block by block! Splendid.
Let us review what you have learned in these ruins.

quickSteps.text: Cross the bridge to the Grand Laboratory
quickSteps.hint: Walk north across the restored stone bridge.
reminder: Calcium carbonate — CaCO₃ — is in chalk and seashells. The bridge ahead is made of it. Hurry on to Dr. Matter!

complete: The bridge is whole again. Breaking limestone into pieces is a physical change — it is still calcium carbonate!
Dr. Matter awaits you in the Grand Laboratory, just beyond the archway.
idle: These fossils are the remains of sea creatures. Their shells were made of calcium carbonate!
When vinegar touches limestone it fizzes. That is a CHEMICAL change: new substances form, including carbon dioxide.

name: The Grand Laboratory
chemistry: Review of everything, plus conservation of matter

dialogue: So YOU are the apprentice who restored the water, melted the gate, powered the pipes and rebuilt the bridge!
I am Dr. Matter, head scientist of the Elemental Dungeon.
Our central reactor has failed, and the vault door to the surface is sealed tight.
To restart it, you must pass the Grand Laboratory's challenges. The stations are marked on your objective list.
Element storage lines both walls, and the advanced crafting tables are on the west side. Good luck!

steps.text: Formula Master: deliver compounds to the console
steps.hint: Right click the green-screen console on the west side to see which compounds it wants. Craft them from memory!
reminder: The Formula Console on the west side will tell you what to craft. No recipes — trust your memory!

steps.text: Sort substances at the Sorting Station
steps.hint: The Sorting Station is on the east side. Element = one kind of atom. Compound = different atoms chemically combined. Mixture = substances mixed but not combined.
reminder: Sort each substance: element, compound or mixture. The station is on the east side.

steps.hint: Count atoms on both sides. You need the same number of H atoms and O atoms on each side.
reminder: Matter is conserved: atoms are never created or destroyed in a reaction. Make both sides match!

dialogue: Before the reactor can start, I must be sure of your mastery. A few review questions!

steps.hint: Each socket's clue describes a compound you have made. Right click a socket to read its clue, then insert the right compound.
reminder: Read each socket's clue. It describes a compound you already know!

steps.text: Walk through the vault into the sunlight
steps.hint: The vault door is open! Climb the stairs to the surface.
reminder: The vault is open! Up the stairs and into the sunshine with you!

complete: You've restored the Elemental Dungeon using the power of chemistry!
From the water we drink to the salt on our food, chemistry is everywhere!
You are officially a MASTER OF MATTER!
idle: Atoms are never created or destroyed in a chemical reaction — they are only rearranged.
Every substance you made today shares the same building blocks: atoms of elements.
